title: Chemical Kinetics
seo_title: Chemical Kinetics Class 12 Chemistry Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 3)
standard_text: Rate of a reaction (average and instantaneous), factors affecting rate of reaction: concentration, temperature, catalyst; order and molecularity of a reaction, rate law and specific rate constant, integrated rate equations and half-life (only for zero and first order reactions), concept of collision theory (elementary idea, no mathematical treatment), activation energy, Arrhenius equation.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Chemistry worksheets for NCERT Chapter 3 Chemical Kinetics: rate of reaction, rate laws, order and molecularity, integrated rate equations, half-life, activation energy and the Arrhenius equation. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

The rate of reaction is the change in concentration per unit time. The rate law rate = k[A]x[B]y is found by experiment; x + y is the order. For a first-order reaction k = (2.303/t) log([R]₀/[R]) and t½ = 0.693/k, independent of concentration; for zero order t½ = [R]₀/2k.

Molecules react only when they collide with energy above the activation energy and in the right orientation. The Arrhenius equation k = A e−Ea/RT explains why rates rise with temperature; catalysts lower Ea.

Example

k = 0.0693 s⁻¹. t(½)?

0.693 ÷ 0.0693

Answer: 10 s

Example

After 3 half-lives?

(½)³

Answer: 0.125

Common mistakes

  • Confusing order and molecularity.
  • Using 0.693/k for zero order.
  • Forgetting that the half-life of first order is independent of concentration.

faq.q: What is the difference between order and molecularity?
faq.a: Order comes from the experimental rate law and can be zero or fractional; molecularity is the number of particles in an elementary step and is a whole number.

faq.q: Why does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
faq.a: It provides an alternative path with a lower activation energy.
